title: Old North Church bells

place.label: Old North Church (Christ Church), Boston
place.coords_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim lookup of the named site (ODbL)

mass_note: tenor 1,545 lb (Old North); all eight more than 5,000 lb (Boston Landmarks Commission)

timeline.event: Bells contracted from Abel Rudhall of Gloucester
Cast in England by the Rudhall foundry (the same report also says 1745 once)
Installed at Christ Church: the first change-ringing bells in the British American colonies
Two signal lanterns are hung in the church's bell tower before the British march
Restored for the Boston Bicentennial (church page)

tiers.everyday: The eight bells of Boston's Old North Church were cast in England in 1744. They were the first ring of change-ringing bells in North America.
tiers.student: The Boston Landmarks Commission records eight bells cast in 1744 by the Rudhall foundry of Gloucestershire and installed in 1745, more than 5,000 lb in all, the first change-ringing bells in the British American colonies; NPS calls them the nation's first maiden peal. Old North gives a 1,545 lb tenor; NPS notes that Paul Revere rang bells there as a teenager and that the 1775 lantern signal was shown from this bell tower. The NPS-archive tower report records rehanging in 1894.
